title: Terraform State Locking Under Concurrent CD: Race Conditions, Backend Contention, and the Partial-Apply Trap
description: How Terraform state locking fails under concurrent CD pipelines, the partial-apply trap, and backend-specific contention mechanics with Go-informed mitigations.
linkedin_post:
Terraform's state lock is not the correctness guarantee most CD pipelines treat it as.

The lock prevents two applies from writing simultaneously. It does not prevent two plans from reading stale state before either acquires the lock—and applying a diff computed against state that has since advanced.

I wrote a deep-dive on the mechanics behind this:

→ How DynamoDB conditional writes implement the lock, and the crash window between S3 PutObject and DynamoDB DeleteItem
→ The partial-apply trap: an apply that returns exit code 0 but applies a diff computed against stale state, producing divergence the state file doesn't expose
→ Why drift detection silently breaks when this happens—terraform plan will agree with the corrupted state
→ A Go-based serial validation gate that reads state from S3, compares serials before applying, and aborts with a re-plan signal instead of silently applying a stale diff
→ When workspace isolation fixes the problem structurally, and when a FIFO apply queue at the orchestration layer is the right answer
→ A post-apply zero-diff assertion as a mandatory pipeline gate

The decision framework at the end maps CD velocity and environment topology to the appropriate locking strategy.

If you're running Terraform inside any real CD pipeline with multiple concurrent triggers, the default locking assumptions are worth pressure-testing.
